verdict.line: You win if you abuse levels 3-5 and the gaps between his Rupture casts to force early kills; you lose if the game drags past level 6 and his Feast stacks turn him into a true-damage wall.

brief.thesis: Fiora holds the structural lane edge and the solo-kill edge here, which lines up with the 50.7% baseline she posts in this lane overall. But against this specific opponent that edge shrinks to a 45.9% win rate over 148 games, because Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture) punishes the exact dash range Fiora needs for Q (Lunge), and once he hits 6 his R (Feast) is a point-and-click true-damage check on any extended trade. The matchup is won in the levels-3-to-5 window before Feast exists, not by grinding it out late.

theirWindow.what: Stay outside the 950-range telegraph and don't extend into melee; if he also lands W (Feral Scream, 300 range) the silence stops you from reactively casting W (Riposte) or Q (Lunge), so disengage rather than trade through it.

yourWindow.when: Right after his Rupture (Q) whiffs or lands
yourWindow.what: Close the gap immediately with Q (Lunge), chain the free second dash, and pop E (Burst of Speed) to snowball move speed off each landed hit. You have roughly 9 seconds before Rupture is back up, so force the full combo in that window rather than trickle damage.

start.why: 92.4% pick rate and the AD/sustain lets you trade autos into his Vorpal Spikes chip without losing the HP race before level 3.

boots.why: 69.6% pick rate; cuts the Feral Scream silence duration and softens the magic damage from Scream plus his passive Spikes proc, which is the actual damage source bleeding you in melee range.

core.why: Sustain and AoE-free single-target damage to win the extended duel before Feast comes online.
Move speed and burst damage to capitalize on the E (Burst of Speed) snowball window while he's still catchable.
Converts Feast's true damage and Rupture poke into delayed damage so a single burst from him doesn't end the fight outright.

situational.when: you're already ahead early and want to force a kill through his shield-adjacent burst before level 6
he's building HP and you need sustained damage through sheer max-health stacking
his magic damage from Feral Scream and Vorpal Spikes is adding up and you need the shield plus AD

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive damage and healing rewards the extended auto-trades you want to force before his Feast exists at 6. Master-tier Fiora players instead run Press the Attack across 2,792 games, which suits a more all-in, burst-then-reset playstyle rather than grinding stacks in a drawn-out duel — take it if you plan to one-shot off level-3 all-ins instead of out-sustaining him.

summoners.why: 84.7% pick rate and it directly converts your levels-3-5 solo-kill advantage into an actual kill before Feast comes online at 6. Flash+Teleport posts a higher 54.5% win rate if you'd rather play the split-push macro and avoid committing to early all-ins.

playing.title: Force all-ins at level 3-5
playing.detail: This is your real window per the data; W (Riposte) and E (Burst of Speed) are both online and his R (Feast) isn't, so a clean parry into a double Q (Lunge) should kill or force a flash.

playing.title: Hold Riposte, don't preemptively cast it
playing.detail: W (Riposte) only pays off if it actually parries his auto or a targeted hit; throw it early and the AD buff is the only thing you get, which isn't enough to win the trade alone.

playing.title: Respect the 300-range Scream silence
playing.detail: Feral Scream silences for a few seconds on a 13s cooldown; if you're silenced mid-combo you can't cast W or Q to finish, so commit your cooldowns before you're inside that range, not after.

playing.title: Treat level 6 as a reset, not a loss
playing.detail: Once Feast (175 range, 60s cooldown) is live, don't sit below 50% HP near him; the true damage ignores your armor stacking from Death's Dance's mitigation entirely.

playing.title: Punish Rupture whiffs immediately
playing.detail: A missed Q (Rupture) is a 9-second window with no poke or knockup threat; that's when your double-Lunge all-in is safest.

playing.title: Don't let the game drag past 12
playing.detail: Each Feast kill grows his max HP (up to 6 stacks), and the overall 45.9% win rate reflects exactly this late-game HP scaling outpacing your duel power. Close the lane or push your split advantage before that compounds.

playing.title: Track his mana for Rupture spam
playing.detail: Rupture is mana-gated early; a few failed casts in a row means he's low and can't zone you off CS, which is your cue to walk up and farm freely.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample-size numbers above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and timing windows are my own read of the matchup, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Use [Q] to strike [P] while dodging Cho’Gath’s (Q). You will have the upper hand if you manage to hit him with [W], allowing you to close in and deal damage.
